$comment: Runtime configuration, fetched by src/main.js on every load with cache: no-cache.
Source delivery declares Remote locations here and pins executable bytes in index.html.
Production delivery composes independently verified Remote artifact reports into this
manifest and the shell integrity import map; Remote implementation bytes never enter
the shell bundle.
Remote entries are loaded by absolute URL through dynamic import(). A Remote may use
only its exact shared bare-specifier interface; the production shell emits facade URLs
for those specifiers. Central governance of shared versions is the feature.
$remotes-comment: Two blocks per remote, and they are not the same thing.
requires  Access control on the mount path. The shell turns it into a route guard,
which the router runs BEFORE `load`, so a user who does not satisfy it
never downloads the remote's code. Absent means the remote is public.
grants    Least privilege for the remote's host context. `api` lists the same-origin
path prefixes it may call through host.auth.fetch; anything else throws
before a request is made. `permissions` is the set it may ask about, so
host.auth.permissions() returns that set intersected with the session's
scopes and the remote learns nothing about the user's other entitlements.
`billing` declares neither: it calls no API and asks about no permission. It still
receives a context and routes its sub-views off it — routing and translation are not
grants, they are what every remote gets.

remotes.$comment: Built on the shell's own stack: imports lit, the signal library and two elements from the shared collection by the specifiers index.html declares. Public, granted nothing, routed through the host context like every other remote.
remotes.name: billing

remotes.$comment: Shares nothing with the shell: no bare specifiers, no Lit, no signals. It reaches the session only through the capabilities granted below, and the server checks the same scope on every request it makes.
remotes.name: analytics

$comment: Locale is a runtime value, not a build target: one deployment for every language, and
setLocale() re-renders every mounted component from its signal.
bundles are URL patterns merged in order, so a micro-frontend can register its own
translations at load time without the shell knowing they exist.
ar is deliberately incomplete. Fallback is per key, so what is missing renders in
English while the layout still flips to rtl.
Where the API is, and nothing else. Which authentication strategy this
application uses is a decision in src/main.js, and what its endpoints are
called is a fact in src/auth/bff-cookie-store.js. Neither is manifest data:
the library admits this document, and a key here would be the library
asserting a contract with a backend it cannot see.
This application uses `bff`, and example/server/auth.mjs is the backend half
— an HttpOnly session cookie, a readable CSRF token, and an access window
that really does expire so AuthSession.fetch() exercises refresh-and-retry.
